issues.legal_issue: A later land-grabbing proceeding is barred by res judicata when a competent court has finally determined the same parties’ substantial dispute over the identity and title of the same property.
material_facts: An earlier specific-performance proceeding finally determined that the disputed land was part of one survey parcel and distinct from the other parcels later claimed by the opposing side.
Earlier land-grabbing proceedings concerning the same property were dismissed, and the determination of the property’s identity and ownership attained finality.
A later land-grabbing case again disputed the identity and title of the same property.
The Supreme Court found that the requirements of res judicata were satisfied.
issues.conclusion: The later land-grabbing proceeding was barred by res judicata. The orders refusing to quash it, and the High Court judgment upholding those orders, were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata is a principle of public policy that promotes finality and prevents repeated litigation of the same matter. It is not confined to suits governed by Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and may apply to other proceedings. Its requirements include the same litigating parties, an identical subject matter, a final decision, and a decision by a competent court. A final determination of the same substantial issue cannot be relitigated in a later proceeding. The Court relied on Bombay Gas Co. v. Jagannath Pandurang; Sheoparsan Singh v. Ramanandan Prasad Narayan Singh; Sri Bhavanarayanaswamivari Temple v. Vadapalli Venkata Bhavanarayana Charyulu; Syed Mohd. Salie Labbai v. Mohd. Hanifa; Narayana Prabhu Venkateswara Prabhu v. Narayana Prabhu Krishna Prabhu; and Ramji Gupta v. Gopi Krishan Agrawal. The later proceeding was before the Special Court under Section 8(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982, but the bar arose from res judicata.

rule.if: later_land_grabbing_proceeding and prior_competent_final_adjudication and same_litigating_parties and same_substantial_property_issue

predicates.later_land_grabbing_proceeding: A claimant brought a later proceeding under a special process for adjudicating alleged land grabbing.
predicates.prior_competent_final_adjudication: A court with authority had finally determined the identity or title of the disputed property in an earlier proceeding.
predicates.same_litigating_parties: The parties to the later dispute were the same as, or legally represented by, parties to the earlier adjudication.
predicates.same_substantial_property_issue: The later proceeding disputed the identity or title of the same property that had been substantially determined earlier.

issues.definition: When a later land-grabbing proceeding between the same litigating parties raises a substantial property issue already finally determined by a competent court, the later proceeding is quashed.
